assessment.nobel_worthiness: A transformative empirical account of long-run inequality and wealth concentration, with unusually large consequences for research and public understanding.
assessment.attribution: Piketty, Saez and Zucman form a coherent core for historical distributional data, top-income research and the measurement of hidden wealth.
assessment.maturity: The research program has accumulated extensive data, methodological development and sustained influence over more than two decades.
uncertainties: The breadth of the program makes the appropriate boundary between core contributors and related scholars contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work changed the empirical understanding of how technology and trade reshape local labour markets, occupations and inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn and Hanson provide a closely connected core contribution linking tasks, trade exposure and labour-market adjustment.
assessment.maturity: The evidence has been widely examined, extended and incorporated into central debates on globalization and technological change.
uncertainties: Separating the distinct causal roles of trade, automation and other concurrent changes remains difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative-data research on mobility has made intergenerational opportunity measurable at an unprecedented geographic and institutional scale.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren and Friedman are central to the linked data infrastructure and empirical findings represented by this discovery.
assessment.maturity: The results have generated a large follow-on literature and durable empirical tools, though the program is comparatively recent.
uncertainties: Administrative-data coverage and institutional portability vary across countries.
Causal interpretation of place and policy effects remains an active research frontier.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on agglomeration and cities has supplied a powerful explanation of the spatial concentration of productivity, employment and housing pressures.
assessment.attribution: Glaeser, Duranton and Moretti represent major complementary theoretical and empirical contributions to the modern urban-economics program.
assessment.maturity: The field's central mechanisms and policy relevance have been tested over a long period across many settings.
uncertainties: The intellectual lineage is broad, making a three-person attribution necessarily selective.
Identification of agglomeration spillovers versus sorting remains challenging.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The integration of exhaustible resources, natural capital and inclusive wealth into economic analysis has enduring importance for long-run welfare.
assessment.attribution: Dasgupta and Heal are foundational contributors to the listed framework and can be credited as a focused pair.
assessment.maturity: The theoretical contribution is long established and increasingly pertinent as environmental accounting and biodiversity policy develop.
uncertainties: Valuing biodiversity and natural capital involves unresolved measurement and ethical choices.
The applied empirical implications remain less settled than the theoretical foundations.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The misallocation framework gave a tractable, influential account of how firm-level distortions can generate large productivity and income differences.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh, Klenow and Restuccia are central contributors to the theoretical and quantitative formulation of this research program.
assessment.maturity: It has stimulated extensive measurement, calibration and development work across countries and sectors.
uncertainties: Estimated distortions may capture forces other than policy-induced misallocation.
Quantitative welfare magnitudes are sensitive to modeling and measurement assumptions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The measurement of management practices established organizational capital as a consequential explanation for firm productivity and cross-country performance.
assessment.attribution: Bloom, Van Reenen and Sadun are closely associated with the survey-based measurement agenda and its leading empirical applications.
assessment.maturity: The program has been replicated and extended across firms, countries and policy contexts over many years.
uncertainties: Management measures can be difficult to separate from selection, reporting and broader organizational differences.
The relative credit due to the wider research network is difficult to delimit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Political-economy research on institutions, accountability, fiscal policy and state capacity has reshaped analysis of how political arrangements influence economic outcomes.
assessment.attribution: Persson, Tabellini and Besley are leading and complementary architects of the modern institutional political-economy literature.
assessment.maturity: The contribution is longstanding, theoretically developed and supported by a broad empirical literature.
uncertainties: The field draws on a wide set of earlier and contemporary contributors.
Institutional causation is difficult to identify cleanly across historical and national contexts.
